card.name: Gombhira
card.era: Traditional (post-7th/8th c.; modern form ~150 years old)
card.tagline: Malda's satirical Shiva folk-theatre of dance and song
card.profile: Gombhira (also Gambhira/Gamvira) is a traditional Bengali folk performing art of the Malda district of West Bengal, combining musical theatre, dance, song and satire to address social and regional issues, typically performed by all-male troupes during Shiva-worshipping festivals (Wikipedia; MAP Academy). Its name derives from 'gombhir' (poise/gravity), a quality associated with Shiva; performances traditionally took place between April and June as part of Chaitra Sankranti / Gajan celebrations (MAP Academy). A typical performance unfolds in stages - bandana (invocation to Shiva), dwaita (duet), charyaari, palabandi gaan (provocation) and khabar (reporting) - and in its classic form two performers, one representing Shiva, converse about everyday hardships (Indian Culture portal).
card.insight: Gombhira evolved from the song-and-dance forms of the Koch people of the Malda region and is tied to local mango cultivation and Shiva worship; it survives in Malda and Murshidabad in India and in Dinajpur, Rangpur and Rajshahi in Bangladesh, where grandfather-and-grandson figures critique sociopolitical issues (MAP Academy; Wikipedia).

observation.setting: Rural outdoor area in West Bengal, in a harvested field and village dirt path, with musicians standing nearby.
observation.dancers: A group of dancers wearing large masks and colorful costumes, plus villagers and children dancing in separate scenes.
observation.formation_and_space: Dancers move in a loose line or small group formation on open dirt and grass, travelling slightly back and forth or in place.
observation.posture: Torso upright, knees slightly bent with bouncy weight shifts.
observation.footwork: Bouncing, stepping side to side and small hops in time with the drum beat; exact weight placement obscured by bulky costumes.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held up and out, gesturing, some holding sticks or swords in one hand and flowing ribbons tied to wrists.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso mostly upright with whole-body bouncing and swaying.
observation.partnering: None; solo movement within a group setting.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Small hops, lifting knees, occasional turning in place.
observation.costume_and_props: Large painted wooden masks covering the face/head, beaded necklaces, layered colorful skirts or patterned trousers, arm ribbons, and handheld sticks or swords.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement and weight transfer are obscured by heavy costumes and camera angles.
